summary: The candidate removes the first-build early return, and focused plus independent tests show that initial target-verify graph setup now launches the fused DSA metadata kernel instead of deferring it to first replay. GPU numerical tests pass on gfx950. The exact eight-rank B300/CUDA driver hang could not be reproduced or disproved, so this is a verified source-level warmup fix but not a fully verified end-to-end resolution.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: initial target-verify setup called fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata zero times; second cached-metadata test passed.
Candidate regression: initial target-verify setup warms the fused kernel and cached metadata is not rebuilt; 2 passed.
Real gfx950 execution of DSA decode, target-verify, and draft-extend Triton metadata kernels against independent PyTorch references; 8 tests and 4 subtests passed on each revision.
Independent candidate cases for first-build and cached reuse at batch sizes 1, 2, and 7 plus initial decode setup; 4 passed on candidate and the same 4 failed on base.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 was used. The repository DSA metadata suite executed real Triton kernels and passed 8 tests plus 4 subtests against PyTorch references.

remaining_counterexamples: Eight NVIDIA B300 sm_103 scheduler contexts could still contend or deadlock if they load the module concurrently during startup rather than first request; this environment cannot test that driver behavior.
The complete GLM-5.2 EAGLE Spec V2 Mooncake PD-disaggregated request path was not run because the required weights, topology, and eight GPUs were unavailable.
The report originates from an internal fork, so fork-only behavior may remain outside the prepared base.
remaining_limitations: Hardware was one AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2, not eight NVIDIA B300 sm_103 GPUs with CUDA driver 590.48.01.
No GLM-5.2 weights, Mooncake two-instance PD setup, or TP8/DP8/EP8 topology were available.
No native rebuild was performed because the candidate contains no native C++ or FlyDSL changes.
The source-level lazy-load prerequisite is fixed, but the original CUDA driver deadlock itself remains unverified.
